candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — wrong-site procedure prevention
candidate.educational_objective: For a lateralized procedure such as eye surgery, verify that required site marking is completed by the appropriately accountable licensed practitioner before the procedure and involve the patient whenever possible.

options.A: Proceed because eye surgery does not require site marking when the consent names the correct eye
options.B: Pause progression and ensure the licensed practitioner accountable for the procedure completes the required site-marking process before the procedure
options.C: Mark the left eye independently so the operating schedule is not delayed
options.D: Proceed to the final time-out because the time-out replaces site marking for paired organs

candidate.rationale: Joint Commission site-marking requirements apply when more than one possible procedural location exists and an incorrect site would affect safety or quality; eye surgery is specifically listed as a common example. The site is marked before the procedure by the licensed practitioner ultimately accountable for and present at the procedure, with the patient involved whenever possible. The nurse should therefore pause progression and ensure the required process is completed rather than independently marking outside the defined process or treating the time-out as a substitute.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Joint Commission requires site marking for procedures with multiple possible locations when wrong-site performance would affect safety/quality, lists eye surgery as an example, and specifies who marks the site and when.
candidate.source_document_title: Universal Protocol – Site Marking: What are Joint Commission’s site marking requirements for operative or other procedures?
candidate.source_locator: Standards FAQ — Universal Protocol – Site Marking: minimum conditions requiring site marking; eye surgery example; accountable licensed practitioner; completion prior to procedure; patient involvement whenever possible
candidate.stem: A client is scheduled for elective surgery on the left eye. During preprocedure verification, the nurse notes that no procedure-site mark is present. The client is alert and able to participate. What should the nurse do?
